text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A group of members of parliament from the ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) petition the President, calling for immediate national party elections to resolve a crisis within.

- The two most powerful parliamentary watchdog committees -- Public Accounts and Public Investments -- come under KANU's control following approval of a resolution to change their composition so as to reflect the principle of proportional representation in the house.
- A Finance Bill which will harmonise personal and single tax relief, removing 140,000 Kenyan workers from the direct taxation bracket, sails through its second reading in parliament.
- Doctors at Nairobi Hospital are concerned about the treatment that political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere is receiving from prison warders.

- The High Court nullifies the controversial March elections conducted by the two warring factions of Opposition party FORD-Kenya, and says both groups need a fresh mandate from their followers to lead.
- The Court of Appeal says Central Bank of Kenya should auction the multi-billion-shilling ultra-modern five-star Grand Regency Hotelin Nairobi.

- A Nairobi primary school headmistress flees to Tanzania after her examination candidates go on the rampage, destroying school property for being denied the opportunity to sit for their final year examination.
- The East African Development Bank launches one billion shillings worth of bonds targeted at institutional investors in the Kenyan market.
